Hi Graeme,

Thank you for getting in touch, and congratulations on your upcoming wedding!

I'm happy to let you know that I am available on 5th December 2026 and would love to photograph your ceremony.

From what you've described, with the ceremony followed by photos at various locations around Edinburgh, 3–4 hours of coverage sounds like it would work well.

Please have a look at the wedding photography packages available on my website and let me know which one best suits your plans. If you're unsure, I'd be happy to recommend the most suitable package based on your timeline and requirements.

Could you also let me know what time your ceremony is due to start? As your wedding is in December, daylight is quite limited, so the ceremony time will play an important part in planning your photography. If you're hoping to visit several locations around Edinburgh after the ceremony, it's worth keeping in mind that it gets dark fairly early at that time of year.

I was also wondering what you mean by "various locations around Edinburgh." Do you already have specific places in mind for your couple portraits, or are you looking for recommendations? I'd be happy to suggest some beautiful locations depending on the style of photos you're after.

If you'd like to go ahead with the booking, I'll require a deposit to secure your wedding date in my diary. Once the deposit has been received, your date will be fully reserved.

If you have any questions or would like to discuss your plans in more detail, please don't hesitate to get in touch.

I look forward to hearing from you.

script.title: Choreography
script.content:
Ceremony in the library. Everyone arrives at the hotel 12.25 pm

(Stevie arrives at 12 noon to check music is ok and begins table set up - readings, tea lights etc)

6 attending: Becca, Graeme and their parents
Rebecca’s parents: Sue (Margaret) & Derek Smith
Graeme’s parents: Sheila & John Elliott

Stevie meets with photographer and confirms music is ready and ok

*Guests arrive and mingle inside. Drinks in hand, top ups available for toast? - Yep
2 minutes to go: Graeme is ready. Door usher (if required) ready. Music ready.

Stevie asks guests to turn off mobile phones. Aeroplane mode please (look at Sue:))

CEREMONY TIME: Rebecca arrives. Photos are taken.
Stevie goes out to see Rebecca and checks you are ready.
When ready, Stevie goes back and asks the guests to stand.
This is the cue for the music to start.

script.title: Processional
script.content:
Walk down the aisle accompanied Beethoven: 5 secrets - [The Piano Guys]  
Rebecca accompanied by her dad, Derek
You can greet each other any way you like. Hugs and kisses?
Stance: You can stand centrally, facing each other (holding hands if you wish).
This way, your parents can see you and you can see them (whilst being able to look at me too.)
I stand centrally, further back

Everyone sits and music ends as arranged on the day

script.title: The Unity Candle
script.content:
To represent marriage and family coming together

Dads light candles > Derek lights Rebecca’s candle and passes it to Becca, John does the same for Graeme, and together, you light the pillar candle

script.title: Reading(s)
script.content: EE Cummings: I Carry Your Heart

script.title: Handfasting:
script.content:
Rebecca and Graeme, you will now exchange vows using traditional handfasting.

Scotland’s ancient marriage ritual symbolises love 

and the strength and understanding that comes from the bonds of marriage. 

Together, you are stronger; together, anything is possible.

Your handfasting celebrates all the wonderful things that marriage brings

Sheila is called forward 

and ties the knot around your hands. Stevie directs this at the time.


Following the vows, the ribbons are removed, or you create your infinity knot… 

I SAY: HOLD ON TIGHT TO YOUR RIBBONS, STEP BACK AND PULL!! 

A SALTIRE OR KISS IS CREATED AND EVERYONE CHEERS!

script.title: Poem & The Vows
script.content:
Graeme reads: 

These I Can Promise by Mark Twain I cannot promise you a life of sunshine; I cannot promise riches, wealth, or gold; I cannot promise you an easy pathway That leads away from change or growing old. But I can promise all my heart’s devotion; A smile to chase away your tears of sorrow; A love that’s ever true and ever growing; A hand to hold in yours through each tomorrow.

script.title: Ring exchange
script.content:
Ring bearer - Stevie 

The wedding ring is a circle; a symbol of eternity and strength, co-operation 

and peace. Rebecca and Graeme, you will now exchange rings to celebrate the commitment 

you are making today. 


Stevie presents the open box to Graeme. Graeme takes Rebecca’s ring


Graeme, please take Rebecca’s left hand and repeat these words after me,

Rebecca, I give you this ring as a symbol of my everlasting love.     

Graeme, you may now place the ring on Rebecca's finger.  


Stevie presents the open box toRebecca. Rebecca takes Graeme’s ring


Rebecca, please take Graeme's left hand and repeat these words after me, 

Graeme, I give you this ring as a symbol of my loyalty and love.   

Rebecca, you may now place the ring on Graeme's finger.  


Rebecca and Graeme,

Your wedding rings are precious gifts of love, 

so wear them with happiness and pride. 

They represent your enduring love and commitment to each other. 

As you build your life together, 

you can look upon the rings you have shared, 

and remember the promises you have made today.

script.title: Pronouncement / Declaration
script.content:
Rebecca and Graeme, 

following your heartfelt promises and exchange of vows and rings,

All that now remains is for you to repeat the following declarations 

in the presence of your witnesses and guests. Please hold hands. 


Graeme, I turn to you first, (please repeat the following declaration after me.)

I, Graeme Elliott declare // my endless love and total loyalty // to Rebecca Juliet Smith.


Rebecca, please repeat the following declaration after me,

I, Rebecca Smith // declare my endless love and total loyalty // to Graeme Elliott.

script.title: Signing
script.content:
Background for the signing: Ludovico Einaudi: Experience & Sia - Helium - [Justin Ward]

You go to the table with the document. 

Parents join you, and we all sign the document

Cue the music!

script.title: Recessional
script.content:
CLOSING CEREMONY

We resume our places and close the ceremony 

with a few happy words and a toast


CLOSING WORDS

Love is a promise and a smile.

Love is going the extra mile.

It is thoughts turned into action,

Never acting without thought.

Marriage is not later, it is now.


It is saying, “I will try”.

It is staying true for life.

It is someone by your side,

It is togetherness, for life


May you bless each other with the love and respect you deserve.

And with patience, trust and understanding, may to continue to 

prioritise your relationship, and remain loyal to your family and friends. 

If you can do this, love and laughter will always surround you.


Hold on to the people who love you, for they will hold on to you.

On the fun days and ‘the Sundays’, we will be there, now and in the future.


Rebecca and Graeme, on behalf of everyone here, 

I wish you the very best in your lives together. 

Go forward as one with our happiness and love!


 

CAN EVERYBODY PLEASE STAND


Dearest parents, the moment has arrived! 

Without further ado, it is my absolute pleasure and privilege 

to introduce to you, for the very first time,

The wonderful, happy and newly declared…

MR AND MRS ELLIOTT!!

Whoops! Cheers! Applause!!



Immediately after toast/pre exit: Recomposed by Max Richter - Vivaldi - The Four Seasons, 1. Spring

readings.title: EE Cummings: I Carry Your Heart
readings.text:
I carry your heart with me (I carry it in my heart)
I am never without it (anywhere
I go you go, my dear; and whatever is done
by only me is your doing, my darling)

I fear no fate (for you are my fate, my sweet)
I want no world (for beautiful you are my world, my true)
and it’s you are whatever a moon has always meant
and whatever a sun will always sing is you

Here is the deepest secret nobody knows
(here is the root of the root and the bud of the bud
and the sky of the sky of a tree called life; which grows
higher than soul can hope or mind can hide)
and this is the wonder that’s keeping the stars apart

I carry your heart (I carry it in my heart)

• Candid pre-ceremony family moments in the lush indoor-outdoor courtyard and glasshouse bar

Candid walking-away shot down the quiet stone path framed by historic mill buildings and bare winter ivy.

photoLocations.name: Circus Lane
photoLocations.notes: a famously picturesque, cobbled residential mews street located in the affluent Stockbridge neighbourhood of Edinburgh, Scotlan

shots.notes: Iconic framing looking down the curved cobblestone mews with St Stephen's spire rising at the end—winter means far fewer tourists blocking the street.
Intimate close-up portrait tucked beside one of the painted cottage doors and winter greenery.

photoLocations.name: St. Bernard’s Well
photoLocations.notes:
A beautiful Greco-Roman structure houses a well once believed to have healing powers.

St. Bernard’s Well is a gorgeous location situated along the Water of Leith. 

Worth noting that Circus Lane, St. Bernard’s Well and Dean Village are all in a short walking distance of each other.

photoLocations.name: Vennel  Viewpoint
photoLocations.notes: an iconic public alleyway and stone staircase in Edinburgh's Old Town, widely celebrated for offering one of the most breathtaking, perfectly framed vantage points of Edinburgh Castle. Tucked away just off the southwest corner of the bustling Grassmarket square, this historic path effortlessly pairs centuries-old atmosphere with a striking, near eye-level view of the majestic fortress towering over the city.

shots.notes: Standing partway up the stone steps with the historic stone wall framing Edinburgh Castle directly behind you—one of the most iconic wedding angles in the city.
Walking together along the wet winter cobblestones as the colorful storefronts and warm pub lights blur in the background
Symmetrical, regal portraits beneath the grand stone arches and colonnade looking out toward the High Street.
Dramatic wide-angle shot outside the Gothic stone entrance capturing the famous crown spire overhead.
Intimate, quiet portraits inside the 16th-century stone courtyard and spiral stair tower away from the Royal Mile crowds.
Classic upward angle from the ornate green-and-gold Ross Fountain with Edinburgh Castle silhouetted high on the rock above.
Walking hand-in-hand along the garden path with the Scott Monument or Old Town skyline peeking through the winter branches.
